clue.text: Where would-be killers are charged by their victims

definitions.text: Where would-be killers are charged by their victims

parts.words: Where would-be killers are charged by their victims
parts.note: the would-be killers are matadors and their victims are the animals that charge at them in the arena

explanation.surface: A grim courtroom where accused murderers face charges brought by those they attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests legal accusation, but here it means a physical rush: the animal charges the matador.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the arena of a Spanish corrida, where toreadors try to kill animals that rush at them.

clue.text: Hard worker receiving new and appropriate allowance

indicators.note: one piece takes another into its middle, so the worker holds the next letter

parts.note: a busy bee is the proverbial hard worker
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: A diligent employee gets a fresh and fitting pay supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: A state payment such as unemployment money is a welfare allowance.

clue.text: Country with serious German ruler

parts.note: land is a country or nation
grave means serious or solemn

explanation.surface: A nation with a solemn Teutonic sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A count holding territorial sovereignty in the old Holy Roman Empire bore this title.

clue.text: Person out of work on Scottish island

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone unemployed living on a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: TIREE is a small island in Scotland's Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped working for good, typically through age, is a pensioner no longer in employment.

clue.text: Mostly very disturbed in mind? island

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Mostly very disturbed in mind? island', gives N(ERV)OUS as wordplay (VER(y) anagrammed inside NOUS) but 'island' cannot define the answer; the definition looks garbled in OCR and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Mostly very disturbed in mind? island

clue.text: Difficulty I am cutting short throughout

parts.note: a pass is a difficult situation, as in 'things have come to a pretty pass'
shortening 'I am' gives the contraction I'm

explanation.surface: Trouble arises when I keep interrupting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting short' tells you to contract 'I am' to I'M rather than to cut anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'here and there', used in footnotes to mean a reference occurs at many places in a text.

clue.text: Be inquisitive about English reprobate he joined outside

indicators.note: one word goes round the others, so about means surrounding them

parts.note: to pry is to be nosy or inquisitive
a rip is a dissolute rogue or reprobate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nosing into an English scoundrel's affairs, he joined in from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like a container signal but is the definition; 'about' does the surrounding and 'joined' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: The fringe or outer edge of an area is its boundary region, the part on the outside.

clue.text: Painter superior to Constable, it's said

indicators.note: says the word for the police rank is spoken, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: a sergeant is the police rank immediately above a constable

explanation.surface: An artist judged better than John Constable, or so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like the landscape painter, but it is the police rank; John Singer Sargent was an American portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was a celebrated portraitist, so the surname names an artist.

clue.text: Novel that is about leading fighters and hard love

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes round the following pieces, so about means surrounding

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
the van, or vanguard, is the leading part of an army
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A book about front-line soldiers and tough romance.
explanation.walkthrough: IVANHOE is Walter Scott's novel of chivalry, fittingly full of fighting and love.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott's 1819 historical romance set in medieval England bears this title.

clue.text: One didn't run anything after the initial course

definitions.meaning: a horse entered for a race that does not take part
read literally as a dish that is not the first course, i.e. not an appetiser

explanation.definitionFit: A runner that fails to start is a scratched entry; jokingly, any dish other than the appetiser.

clue.text: Somebody's going to hit it

parts.note: to 'hit' this is an idiom for setting off on a journey, so a departing person is about to hit it

explanation.surface: A threat that someone is about to strike a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' suggests violence, but the idiom 'hit the road' means to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The highway is what a traveller is said to hit when departing.

clue.text: Orator's statistic that's not meant to be taken literally

definitions.meaning: read literally, a number quoted in someone's address

definitions.text: that's not meant to be taken literally
definitions.meaning: an expression such as metaphor or simile used non-literally

explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorical device like metaphor is a non-literal expression; jocularly, a number from a lecture.

clue.text: Works as salesman and so becomes broad-minded?

definitions.meaning: a commercial representative goes on the road selling
alludes to the saying that journeying broadens the mind

explanation.definitionFit: A rep journeys around selling; and journeying is said to broaden the mind.

clue.text: Utmost effort shown by joint winners?

definitions.meaning: one's very utmost, as in 'do your ___'
read literally, contestants who tie for first are equal top

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for one's hardest try; literally, sharing the top place equally.

clue.text: A little drink of wine used to make a guy secure

definitions.text: used to make a guy secure

parts.note: tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine
a peg is a small measure of spirits, especially in old Anglo-Indian use

explanation.surface: A small tot of wine is just the thing to keep a fellow steady.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'guy' is not a man but a guy rope; 'of' links the drink to the wine that precedes it in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake driven into the ground holds the rope that braces a camping shelter.

clue.text: Form of praise she found in old sect

indicators.note: a new form of the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman discovers a style of worship in an ancient religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: This strict Jewish party of Second Temple times was an ancient religious faction.

clue.text: Source of combs for dated hairstyle

definitions.meaning: honeycombs are built by bees in their home
a tall rounded bouffant fashionable in the 1960s

explanation.definitionFit: Bees' nest produces honeycomb; also a towering 1960s women's coiffure.

clue.text: Play the final moves

definitions.meaning: the closing phase of a chess game

explanation.definitionFit: A Beckett drama bears this title, and chess players use it for the closing stage.

clue.text: He wasn't bound to complete his performance

definitions.text: He wasn't bound to complete his performance

parts.words: He wasn't bound to complete his performance
parts.note: describes a famous escapologist who was tied up at the start of each act but free of his bonds by its end

explanation.surface: A performer who was under no obligation to finish his show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'obliged', but it means tied up in chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry the escape artist ended every act free of the ropes and shackles.

clue.text: One way to remember how circulation is maintained

definitions.meaning: learning something by rote, from memory
read literally, blood is pumped round the body by the cardiac organ

explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote means memorising; literally, blood circulates thanks to the cardiac pump.

clue.text: Source of boom' in freezing North

parts.note: bitter means bitterly cold

explanation.surface: Something booms out in the icy north.
explanation.definitionFit: This marsh bird of the heron family is known for its deep, booming call.

clue.text: Old soldier fired in anticipation

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other

parts.note: hope is expectation or anticipation
lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: A veteran shot with eager expectation.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavily armed infantryman of ancient Greece was a citizen soldier of antiquity.

clue.text: Powerful man's pronouncement to increase tension

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word for the strong man is said out loud

parts.note: a titan is a person of great strength or power

explanation.surface: A strongman's declaration ratchets up the pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something tauter is to increase its tension.

clue.text: Playing technique in tennis match — excellent

parts.note: doubles is a tennis match with two players a side
topping is old British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A clever stroke in an outstanding tennis game.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPPING is dated British slang for 'excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowing two strings at once on a violin or cello is a method of playing.

clue.text: Egyptian servant returning garment for Indian

indicators.note: returning means the servant's name is read backwards

parts.note: Iras is one of Cleopatra's attendants in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: An Egyptian domestic comes back with clothing for an Indian.
explanation.walkthrough: IRAS is one of Cleopatra's maids in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: A long draped cloth wrapped round the body is traditional women's dress in India.

clue.text: Authority imprisoning one with soldiers after trial

indicators.note: one piece locks the others inside it

parts.note: an expert is an authority on a subject
I is the Roman numeral for one
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A judge locks up someone along with troops after a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' looks like a court case, but it is the definition in the sense of a test; 'after' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientific test conducted to check a hypothesis is a trial.

clue.text: One quarter are discriminatory, in a way

parts.note: south is one of the four quarters or compass points, abbreviated S
to exist is to be, so exist can stand for are

explanation.surface: A fourth of them are biased in some respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice against one gender is one particular kind of discrimination.

clue.text: Author who was nominally but not primarily Christian

definitions.text: Author who was nominally but not primarily Christian

parts.words: Author who was nominally but not primarily Christian
parts.note: the fairy-tale writer Hans Christian had Christian in his name, but as his middle name, not his first

explanation.surface: A writer who was a Christian in name only, not at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nominally' means 'in name' literally, and 'not primarily' means it was not his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian, the Danish teller of fairy tales, is the writer described.
